MORGAN STANLEY ON GLOBAL AI SECTOR ; BUY THE DIP | AI INVESTMENT OPPORTUNITIES POST US MIDTERMS

• AI CAPEX GUIDANCE UNCHANGED: Maintains hyperscaler capex forecasts of $1.67 trillion in 2027 and $1.76 trillion in 2028.

• DATA CENTRE DELAYS: Expects around 20% of US data-centre projects scheduled for 2028 to shift into 2029, equivalent to 5 GW of capacity.

• 2027 OUTLOOK INTACT: Texas election results and new data-centre approval processes unlikely to disrupt projects already under construction.

• CAPACITY GROWTH: US data-centre capacity additions expected to decline 4% YoY in 2028 before surging 38% in 2029.

• GLOBAL SPILLOVER: Project delays in the US could redirect around 20 GW of potential data-centre development towards Asia and EMEA.

• POWER SHORTAGE: Morgan Stanley's AI model indicates over 30% power-capacity shortfall through 2028, supporting demand for existing operational data centres.

• AI EFFICIENCY: Meta targets 10x improvement in compute efficiency in 2027; TPU advancements could further improve AI training and inference economics.

• TOP HYPERSCALER PICKS: Overweight Amazon, Meta and Alphabet, supported by scale, capital access and AI infrastructure advantages.

• AI INFRASTRUCTURE PICKS: Favours Equinix and selected powered-shell providers amid infrastructure bottlenecks.

• DATA CENTRE RISKS: US permitting restrictions, higher development costs and slower project approvals could pressure 2028 infrastructure orders.

• KEY STRATEGY: Views the recent AI-stock correction as overdone; recommends selectively buying hyperscalers, infrastructure companies and AI software enablers.

• LONG-TERM VIEW: Believes project delays could extend the AI investment cycle rather than derail it, favouring well-capitalised technology leaders.

US GOVERNMENT SHUTDOWN RISK RISES OVER IRAN WAR

Congressional Democrats are considering using the December 11 government funding deadline to pressure President Trump to end the war with Iran, Bloomberg reports.

Democrats could block spending legislation or restrict funding for military operations, potentially triggering another federal government shutdown.

The party faces a choice between acting immediately or waiting until January, when Democrats take control of both chambers of Congress.

The Pentagon is also seeking at least $350 billion in additional funding, complicating negotiations.

WHIRLPOOL OF INDIA Q2 FY27: REVENUE UP 14% YOY TO ₹1,873 CR; EBITDA MARGIN AT 2.1% AMID COST PRESSURES, ANNOUNCES 5% PRICE HIKE & PREMIUM PRODUCT EXPANSION

• EBITDA: Stood at ₹40 Cr, with margin at 2.1%, down 140 bps YoY.

• PBT: ₹34 Cr before exceptional items, with margin at 1.8%, down 110 bps YoY.

• Margin Pressure: Higher commodity costs, crude oil prices, currency depreciation, energy regulations and new product investments impacted profitability.

• Price Hike: Implemented an additional approximately 5% price increase effective November 1, 2026, to offset inflationary pressures.

• Premium Product Launch: Introduced Luxuriem, a premium 654-litre, four-door refrigerator range.

• Elica India: Subsidiary revenue grew 12% YoY, while PBT increased 22%.

• Cost Optimisation: P4G productivity programme and strategic pricing actions aimed at improving operating efficiency.

• Management Outlook: Focused on sustaining revenue growth through premiumisation, pricing actions and productivity improvements while protecting margins against rising input costs.

US AND IRAN CONSIDER $8 BILLION DEAL TO REOPEN STRAIT OF HORMUZ

President Trump is expected to meet Qatar's prime minister Monday to discuss an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for releasing $8 billion in frozen funds, according to Israel Hayom.

The reported deal would end Iranian attacks on Gulf shipping and lift US restrictions, but would not address Iran's nuclear program.

Vice President JD Vance is reportedly pushing for an agreement despite opposition from senior administration officials.

NVIDIA ESPIONAGE REPORTS COULD TRIGGER TOUGHER US CHIP EXPORT RESTRICTIONS

Raymond James warns that reports of alleged Chinese espionage targeting Nvidia ($NVDA ) could accelerate congressional support for the MATCH Act, which would tighten semiconductor and chipmaking equipment exports to China.

The legislation has bipartisan backing, with incoming Democratic congressional majorities potentially pushing for even stricter controls.

Additional restrictions could threaten the fragile US-China trade détente, particularly China's continued supply of rare earth minerals.

CITI DOWNGRADES US STOCKS AND TECH, TURNS BULLISH ON EUROPE

Citi has downgraded US equities, global technology and European technology to Neutral, citing weakening AI sentiment and risks of further investor selling.

The bank warns that the Nasdaq could fall another 5% before positioning turns decisively bearish.

Despite remaining constructive on AI over the medium term, Citi wants more stable sentiment and earnings expectations before turning bullish again.

Meanwhile, European equities excluding the UK were upgraded to Overweight, benefiting from lower oil prices and reduced technology exposure.

reports.text:
CITI on Bharti Airtel ; Buy, TP Rs 2390

In a notable reversal, Bharti has reinstated its Rs299 recharge plan 3 months after withdrawing it in Aug'26.

While earlier plan offered 1.5 GB/day of data, relaunched version provides 1 GB/day.

Move reflects Bharti's response to competitive pressures, as peers did not follow its earlier tariff action, as well as elevated churn during 2Q.

Churn increased from 2.6% to 2.9% qoq, resulting in net subscriber additions slowing sharply qoq from +3.3m to +0.7m

Decision underscores challenges of implementing unilateral tariff actions in prepaid smartphone segment, where competitive intensity remains highest

It suggests that pricing discipline is difficult to sustain without broader industry participation.

Note that based on certain assumptions around Bharti's subscriber mix, had estimated the Aug'26 move could potentially benefit ARPU by c.Rs4/mth (EPS benefit of c.2%).

Bharti recently reported ARPU improvement from Rs264 to Rs271 in 2Q.

Indian pharma companies are moving from APIs into peptides, ADCs, CDMO & biosimilars.

Laurus commissioned over 16,000 l of peptide synthesis capacity. can make the complete peptide API.

Its new facility for ADC payloads and linkers is also operational.

Sai Life's first peptide development lab is commissioned. 
Now has 34 commercial programmes and 14 in late phase.

Anthem now has 15 commercial molecules and 9 in Phase three.

Currently sole supplier for 5 molecules commercialised over last 18 months.

Divi's has 18 to 20 custom synthesis project commercial or moving into commercial supply.

Divi's makes its own peptide building blocks, amino acids, resins and fragments.

Navin Fluorine's two dedicated Fermion phases can do 900 to 1000cr annual revenue at peak. 

Phase 2 is targeted for Q4 FY27.

Aarti Pharmalabs has 39 commercial CDMO projects. Working with 23 customers.

Its 405 KL dedicated block for 3 to 4 repeat projects is targeted for H2 FY28.

Shilpa has 4 CDMO programmes under registration. One expected to commercialise in FY28 and three in FY29.

First ADC biosimilar expected to enter human studies in FY28. Payload, linker, antibody and conjugation capabilities in house.

Acutaas now targets 1000cr CDMO revenue in FY27, a year ahead of plan. Targets 2000cr by FY30.

8 to 9 CDMO products expected to start contributing over the next 12 to 18 months.

Senores has 41 approved ANDAs still to launch. Expects these launches over the next 6 to 8 quarters.

Beta Drugs targets around 1000cr revenue by FY30.

BERKSHIRE HATHAWAY Q3: RECORD $9.6 BN SHARE BUYBACK; CASH RESERVES AT $377 BN

• Record Buyback: Berkshire repurchased $9.6 Bn of its own shares in Q3 2026, surpassing its previous quarterly record of $9.3 Bn in Q3 2020

• Buyback Resumption: Company resumed share repurchases in March 2026 after six consecutive quarters without buybacks

• September Purchases: Spent approximately $5.4 Bn repurchasing shares at an average price of $506.64 per Class B share

• FY26 Buybacks: Total share repurchases reached approximately $14.4 Bn during the first nine months of 2026

• Equity Investments: Purchased $2.4 Bn of other companies' shares during Q3 while selling approximately $2.8 Bn, making Berkshire a modest net seller

• Buyback Comparison: Spent four times as much repurchasing its own shares as purchasing other listed equities during Q3

• Cash Reserves: Cash, cash equivalents and short-term Treasury bills stood at approximately $377.4 Bn at September-end

• Operating Earnings: Declined approximately 6% YoY to $12.71 Bn, primarily due to weaker insurance results

• Net Profit: Fell 28% YoY to $22.11 Bn, partly reflecting lower investment gains

• Leadership Strategy: CEO Greg Abel has accelerated share repurchases, reflecting a greater willingness to deploy capital

• Capital Allocation: Aggressive buybacks suggest management sees attractive value in Berkshire shares, while maintaining substantial liquidity for future investments

reports.text:
TATA STEEL Q2 FY27: REVENUE UP 11.5% YOY, EBITDA RISES 17%, PAT JUMPS 16%; INDIA DELIVERIES GROW 16% QOQ, ₹7,140 CR FY27 COST-SAVINGS TARGET & 4.8 MTPA NINL EXPANSION UNDERWAY

• India Business: Revenue at ₹42,653 Cr, with EBITDA of ₹10,634 Cr and margin of 25%.

• Steel Deliveries: Consolidated deliveries reached 7.92 million tonnes, up 9% QoQ; India deliveries surged 16% QoQ to 5.98 million tonnes.

• Automotive Business: Achieved record Q2 volumes of approximately 1.1 million tonnes, supported by 26% growth in high-end sales.

• Cost Savings Guidance: Targets ₹7,140 Cr savings in FY27, with approximately ₹1,793 Cr achieved so far.

• Capacity Expansion: 4.8 MTPA NINL expansion entered execution phase; India steelmaking capacity scalable beyond 40 MTPA.

• Downstream Expansion: Progressing 0.7 MTPA galvanising line, tinplate expansion and other value-added steel projects.

• Netherlands Business: EBITDA improved to €72 Mn from €4 Mn QoQ following Direct Sheet Plant restart.

• UK Business: Reported EBITDA loss of £56 Mn; 3 MTPA electric arc furnace project progressing.

• Capex: Invested ₹6,860 Cr during H1 FY27, including ₹3,280 Cr in Q2.

• Balance Sheet: Net debt at ₹91,423 Cr, net debt/EBITDA at 2.4x and liquidity at ₹40,076 Cr.

• H1 FY27 Performance: Revenue at ₹1,26,231 Cr; EBITDA increased 21% YoY to ₹20,035 Cr.

• Management Outlook: Focused on India volume growth, premium steel products, cost optimisation, downstream expansion and improving European operations, while monitoring raw material costs and global steel market challenges.

- State zoning restrictions threaten infrastructure expansion.

- Currency pressures remain a risk.

Curious when FII will come back to India

So gave Co-pilot a prompt
“Why FIIs wont return to India even as AI trade unwind globally”

Reverse Psychology

Here is the response

1. India is still expensive vs EM peers
o Even after corrections, India trades at a premium to most emerging markets.
o FIIs compare India with China, Korea, Taiwan, Brazil, not with India's own history.
o If China is at 10-12x PE and India at 20-25x PE, capital tends to chase cheaper markets. 
2. India lacks direct AI beneficiaries
o The AI trade created winners in US tech, Taiwan semiconductors and Korean memory-chip companies.
o India has very few large listed AI, semiconductor or hyperscaler plays that global thematic funds can buy. 
3. Dollar returns matter, not rupee returns
o FIIs think in USD.
o Even if Nifty is flat or slightly up, rupee depreciation can wipe out returns.
o Currency risk remains a major deterrent for foreign capital. 
4. US yields remain a strong competitor
o If US Treasuries offer attractive risk-free returns, FIIs need a much higher expected return from India.
o Many global allocators prefer earning 4-5% in dollar assets rather than taking EM risk. 
5. India's earnings growth has moderated
o India's premium valuation was justified when earnings were compounding rapidly.
o If earnings growth slows while valuations remain rich, FIIs question the risk-reward. 
6. Better opportunities elsewhere
o Korea, Taiwan and China offer exposure to AI, semiconductors and manufacturing at lower valuations.
o Global funds have finite capital; India is competing against these markets for allocation. 
7. India is no longer an under-owned market
o After years of strong inflows, most EM funds already have meaningful India exposure.
o Incremental flows require a new catalyst, not just the absence of AI enthusiasm.
8. Domestic flows reduce urgency
o SIPs, mutual funds and insurance money continue supporting Indian markets despite FII selling.
o Paradoxically, this resilience prevents large valuation corrections that would otherwise attract FIIs back.

Maruti Suzuki India should be rechristened as Suzuki India

Maruti's journey started as a Govt of India project. Maruti Udyog was the Indian promoter & Suzuki was brought in as the technology partner. Back then, this was very much an Indian company with Japanese know-how.

Over time, the Indian promoter gradually diluted its holding & eventually exited completely. Suzuki did the opposite, staying invested through every cycle & steadily increasing its stake.

What began as a JV slowly became Suzuki's most important global asset. The ownership story itself tells you who has deepened commitment over the decades.

For years, investors debated why Suzuki was setting up fresh manufacturing capacity outside Maruti Suzuki through its Gujarat subsidiary instead of housing it directly in the listed entity.

Then came the reversal. Suzuki transferred Suzuki Motor Gujarat into Maruti Suzuki at a valuation of roughly ₹12,000+ Cr. Rather than taking cash, it largely took equity.

The result? Suzuki's ownership in Maruti Suzuki moved up further without having to buy equivalent shares from the secondary market.

This wasn't just a restructuring exercise. It was Suzuki effectively converting manufacturing assets into a larger stake in India's largest PV company.

Even after that transaction, Suzuki did not stop. It has periodically picked up additional shares from the open market whenever opportunities emerged.

The message is clear. The Indian promoter exited long ago. The Japanese promoter keeps doubling down on India.

Look at the cars on the road today. The branding emphasis is on the giant "S" logo. 10-15years back, cars started selling with only “S” logo, 1st on premium nexa cars, then on all the models. You will hardly see Maruti branded cars on road now

For many younger buyers, the brand recall is shifting from "Maruti Suzuki" to simply "Suzuki". The transition is subtle but visible.

India is now the crown jewel of Suzuki Motor Corp. A substantial portion of Suzuki valuation come from Indian listed entity. Maruti $38bn mcap translate to $21bn (for 58% stake, $15bn if applied 30% Holdco disc).

Even beyond that, Maruti pays over $500m to Suzuki as royalty, that value must be over $5bn in the SoTP of Suzuki motors. Suzuki motors also have successful 2w biz in India, they are 6th largest 2w in India, clocking over 1lac units every month

In many ways, investors buying Suzuki Motor Corp are indirectly buying the India story. Cars sold by Suzuki in India is higher than overall car sold by Suzuki in other 100 countries combined

A rebranding to "Suzuki India" could also help shed the old "cheap small-car company" perception. As premium SUVs, hybrids & future EVs gain share, a stronger global MNC identity may command a different customer mindset.

Ownership, capital allocation, manufacturing integration, branding & growth strategy all point in one direction: this is increasingly Suzuki's India story.

Conclusion: Maruti only stays in Co. name hence should be renamed now
